questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Uruguay?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Uruguay on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Uruguay article.

questions.proof: Uruguay is bordered by two large neighbors, Brazil and Argentina.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Uruguay about 176,215 square kilometres; Nicaragua about 120,340 square kilometres; Trinidad and Tobago about 5,128 square kilometres; Monaco about 2 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Montevideo?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Uruguay is Montevideo.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Uruguay?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Uruguay article.

questions.proof: Its capital and largest city is Montevideo.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Uruguay on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Uruguay on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
